row.evidence: Docebo's SSO docs describe only just-in-time user provisioning (a user logging in via SSO who does not yet exist will be created on the fly); no SCIM endpoint is documented in its help centre or developer portal.
row.notes: Quote-only pricing (Elevate and Enterprise, both 'Get your pricing'; priced on active users). No SCIM found by absence: help-centre search for 'scim' returns no articles, the developer portal index has none, and Okta's catalogue only lists a Docebo Provisioning Connector by Aquera (third party). Automation is SAML/OIDC/Auth0 JIT with attribute updates on login, CSV import/activate/deactivate, Docebo Connect (iPaaS) recipes and the REST manage API (OAuth2). The Enterprise card adds 'Upgraded API access — 100 calls/min', implying API access on Elevate too.

plans.name: Elevate
plans.notes: user_api inferred from the Enterprise card's 'Upgraded API access', which implies Elevate has standard API access.

scim.notes: available=false is by absence: no SCIM documentation found; the vendor never states it explicitly.

endpoints.purpose: Create or update users in batch

rate_limits.text: Token-bucket rate limiting per identity (the authenticated user account); Enterprise card advertises 100 calls/min.

okta.notes: Only OIN result for 'docebo' is the Aquera provisioning connector; okta.com/integrations/docebo/ returns 404. Docebo's own Okta SAML guide covers SSO.

entra.notes: Docebo's Entra guide uses a non-gallery app; learn.microsoft.com docebo-tutorial and docebo-provisioning-tutorial return 404.

onelogin.notes: From Docebo's own OneLogin guide (two Docebo apps in the OneLogin catalogue); OneLogin's page not loaded.

fallbacks.other_sync: Docebo Connect (iPaaS) recipes, Salesforce user sync, HRIS integrations
